drivers.text: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41.0B in equity value, funded with cash and new debt. Insmed closed at $170.15, below the offer, and Sanofi's US shares rose 11.0%.

sowhat.text: Two large deals in two days, Sanofi and Insmed in cash and CrowdStrike and Zscaler in stock, show strategics will still write big checks despite chip volatility. Sanofi is using new debt, with the 10-year at 4.91% and high yield at 363 bp on Monday.

pitch: Stocks slipped Tuesday after Monday's big rebound. The S&P 500 fell half a percent to about 7,200 and the Nasdaq fell 1.5 percent as chip stocks gave back gains, with Micron down 11 percent. The Dow rose almost 1 percent. The 10-year was about 4.91 percent, and the Fed meets December 8 and 9. Oil bounced, with WTI up 2.3 percent to about 82 dollars and Brent at 91. On deals, Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for about 41 billion dollars in cash, funded partly with new debt, a day after CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about 44 billion in stock.

quiz.q: Where did the S&P 500 close on Tue 24 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq fall 1.5% on 24 Nov?
quiz.a: Chip stocks gave back part of Monday's rally: Micron fell 11.0%, AMD 8.9% and Nvidia 5.9%.

quiz.q: What is Sanofi paying for Insmed, and in what form?
quiz.a: $175 a share in cash, about $41.0B in equity value.

chat.a: Tuesday was a pullback: the S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,201 and the Nasdaq fell 1.5%, as Micron, AMD and Nvidia gave back part of Monday's rally. The Dow rose 0.9%. The VIX was 26.36 and the 10-year was 4.91%.
chat.tip: Lead with the chip reversal, then note the Dow held up.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $82.05, up 2.3%, and Brent at $91.40, up 2.3%, a spread of about $9. That recovers part of Monday's drop. For energy M&A, a steadier price helps buyers and sellers agree on value.
chat.tip: Give the level and direction, then stop.

chat.a: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41.0B, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $43.9B in stock. Neither release named advisers.
chat.tip: Say the advisers were not disclosed rather than guess.

chat.q: What are you watching over the next few weeks?
chat.a: The Dec 8-9 FOMC, with the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% and the 10-year at 4.91%. Before that, Wednesday's GDP and PCE data, and whether chips stabilize after the Thanksgiving break.
chat.tip: Tie each event to financing conditions.

chat.q: Why would Sanofi fund Insmed with cash and debt rather than stock?
chat.a: A cash offer gives Insmed holders a fixed $175 a share, so there is no exposure to Sanofi's share price. It costs Sanofi new debt when the 10-year is 4.91%. Insmed closed at $170.15, below the offer, which reflects time to close and regulatory risk.
chat.tip: Say fixed value for the seller, leverage for the buyer.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.91% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How would you describe credit markets right now?
chat.a: High yield was 363 bp and investment grade 97 bp on Monday, both slightly tighter than Friday. That is still a functioning market for acquisition financing, though Tuesday's reading is not yet published. Sanofi's committed debt financing shows large buyers can still borrow.
